translation_notes: URIRef('http://example.org/count') -> <http://example.org/count> and Literal('not-a-number', datatype=XSD.integer) -> "not-a-number"^^xsd:integer, both as bare islands in operand position inside the existing tuple; the statement keeps its shape

no g{} island: np.pubinfo is a read-only property on Nanopub, so `np.pubinfo += g{ … }` (which rebinds the attribute) cannot be used - the draft's version would raise AttributeError. Term islands inside the original .add((s, p, o)) call are the faithful form here. Worth noting as a limit of the `graph += g{}` idiom

XSD -> @prefix xsd: ; the other namespaces the test module imports (DC, RDF, DCTERMS, PROV) are unused in the region, so no prefixes are declared for them (the draft declared five, injected inside the `from tests.conftest import (` statement, which does not parse)

context shims (identical for both sides): test_nanopub_context.py carries _minimal_valid_nanopub verbatim (tests/test_nanopub.py lines 763-773 - the region calls it but the extraction dropped it); tests/conftest.py is an offline stand-in for the upstream conftest, which downloads the nanopub test suite and probes the nanopub server; the rsa-key1 key pair is vendored under testsuite/ (nanopub-testsuite, MIT)
the nanopub package is not installed in the evaluation venv; driver.py appends the corpus checkout to sys.path, after the example directory, so the local `tests` package wins over the corpus one

driver replaces pytest's monkeypatch fixture by a recording stand-in with the same .setattr, comparable by value (pytest's MonkeyPatch compares by identity, which the harness would report as a difference); like the region intends, nothing is undone
equivalence evidence is the region's own pytest.raises(..., match='not-a-number'): the error carries that message only if the pubinfo triple really holds 'not-a-number' typed as xsd:integer
